purpose: Create the third scaled-agent lane-depth and public-explainability packet set for the Wave 3 public-good lanes: Disaster and resilience, Justice/courts/public safety, and Science/energy/environment.

lane_packets.what_it_does: Tracks federal disaster relief, insurance, recovery, mitigation, and resilience commitments while separating event response, recurring exposure, base funding, supplemental funding, and mitigation investments before any cost or reserve conclusion.

what_taxpayers_pay_now.required_next: official multi-year disaster path, base-versus-supplemental funding bridge, event-to-account-to-outlay crosswalk, exposure denominators, damage records, mitigation methods, and reserve-rule parameters

lane_packets.who_is_served_or_protected: People, households, businesses, tribes, states, territories, local governments, infrastructure owners, and communities affected by disasters, plus taxpayers exposed to recurring federal disaster costs.
lane_packets.overspending_underfunding_boundary: Large supplemental outlays, repeated declarations, high exposure, or weak mitigation linkage are review-needed signals only. They are not savings estimates, waste findings, fraud findings, cut instructions, or evidence that aid should be reduced.
lane_packets.technology_transition_boundary: Claims intake, damage inspection, grant management, geospatial risk mapping, benefit delivery, procurement, fraud/error controls, privacy, cybersecurity, appeals, and offline emergency fallback capacity must be costed before any modernization credit.
lane_packets.event_and_mitigation_boundary: Declarations are not spending, mitigation project amounts are not federal outlays, benefit-cost ratios are not realized savings, and GAO high-risk status is not a savings estimate, waste finding, or fraud finding.

lane_packets.what_it_does: Tracks federal justice, courts, law enforcement, corrections, and criminal-justice assistance while keeping federal activity separate from dominant state and local policing, courts, corrections, and public-safety systems.

what_taxpayers_pay_now.required_next: official multi-year justice path, state/local spending bridge, caseload denominators, court timeliness, correctional safety, crime/victimization outcomes, and rights floors

lane_packets.who_is_served_or_protected: The public, victims, defendants, detained and incarcerated people, court users, law-enforcement and correctional staff, state/local partners receiving federal grants, and communities affected by safety and rights outcomes.
lane_packets.overspending_underfunding_boundary: Caseload pressure, grant patterns, crime outcomes, or correctional conditions are review-needed signals only. They are not savings estimates, waste findings, fraud findings, or instructions to cut courts, law enforcement, public defense, corrections, or grants.
lane_packets.technology_transition_boundary: Court filing systems, case management, records exchange, evidence systems, jail/prison operations, grant monitoring, privacy, cybersecurity, bias controls, due process, and public access must be costed before any modernization credit.
lane_packets.federalism_boundary: Federal function 750 excludes most state/local policing, prosecution, courts, corrections, and public safety and mixes distinct constitutional and operational purposes.
lane_packets.comparison_boundary: A peer comparison must not rank raw recorded crime alone. International differences are not savings, and peer spending differences cannot populate target-cost fields.

lane_packets.what_it_does: Tracks federal science, space, technology, energy, natural-resource, and environmental commitments while keeping science, energy, and environment component scenarios separate before any aggregate use.

what_taxpayers_pay_now.required_next: official multi-year paths and separate component scenarios for science, energy, and environment with state/local, tax-expenditure, and outcome bridges

lane_packets.who_is_served_or_protected: Researchers, students, energy users, communities, resource users, environmental beneficiaries, grid and reliability stakeholders, future generations, and taxpayers funding public R&D, energy, and environmental commitments.
lane_packets.overspending_underfunding_boundary: Component cost or peer differences are review-needed signals only. The lane has no composite efficiency target, and science, energy, and environment differences are not savings, waste findings, fraud findings, or instructions to cut missions.
lane_packets.technology_transition_boundary: R&D portfolios, grid modernization, energy systems, environmental monitoring, permitting systems, data infrastructure, cybersecurity, adoption lags, and mission continuity must be costed before any technology credit.
lane_packets.component_separation_boundary: Science, energy, and environment require separate component scenarios. This scaffold publishes no composite target and no composite rank.

plain_english_status: Wave 3 now has public-good lane-depth explainability scaffolds for Disaster and resilience, Justice/courts/public safety, and Science/energy/environment. These packets explain what each lane does, who is served, what outcomes matter, where overspending or underfunding review signals may arise, and what technology transition work would need to be modeled. They do not complete lane depth, calculate rates, publish target costs, claim savings, identify waste or fraud, direct department cuts, claim technology savings, run the solver, or claim a balanced budget.
